aggressive_definition: High-grade prostate cancer defined as grade group 3–5.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Multivariable logistic regression was used to test the association between alcohol intake across decades and diagnosis of overall, low-grade [grade group (GG) 1-2] and high-grade prostate cancer (GG 3-5).
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Of 650 men ages 49-89 who underwent biopsy, 325 were diagnosed with prostate cancer, 238 with low-grade and 88 with high-grade disease.
reason: The biopsy cohort analyzes diagnosis of both overall prostate cancer and high-grade prostate cancer, with high-grade disease explicitly defined as grade group 3–5. It is not established as a prospective cohort analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Relative to nondrinkers, men who consumed ≥7 drinks/week at ages 15 to 19 had increased odds of high-grade prostate cancer diagnosis (OR = 3.21, P trend = 0.020), with similar findings for ages 20 to 29, 30 to 39, and 40 to 49.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate explicitly concerns high-grade prostate cancer diagnosis. Although the supplied confidence limits were calculated outside the abstract, the aggressive endpoint itself is directly supported by the abstract.
